# Root author-side check: two rows exclude the fixed complementary-degree template

2026-10-15. This is a proposed exact coefficient check for the original
CM24 support author, not an independent review. Original owner
EM-DIRECT-18F24A and support EM-CM24CONN-63E74C9D remain unchanged.
The source Gauss parameters and top rows require their separate check.
No full-target evaluation or parent no-go is claimed.

Use the preceding complementary-degree R, with d=4m, n=2m,
p=6m+1, L_n R=P_n/9 and R(1)=0. Define the even cubic pullback

    U(x)=R(S(sqrt(x))), S(r)=4r^3-3r,
    u=[x^(p-1)]U !=0,
    N=3m=(p-1)/2, sigma=1-2g.

The support author's fixed source-only template is

    k=(g-4sigma/5)/u,
    Z_R=k[U-U(0)-u x^(p-1)],
    E=(1-x)Z_R'-(4x^N-2)(H-H_b).

The original full baseline is

    H_b=g(1+x^N)+(4sigma/5)x+(sigma/5)x^(N-1).

There is no free lower correction or input from the complete unknown
target primitive. Exact identity of this particular Z_R with the target
primitive would require E=0 as a polynomial. This is stronger than an
accidental equality of one half-point value and does not exhaust other
possible target relations.

## Four top coefficients of U

The support already derived U's top coefficients u,u/2,5u/16 at
x^(p-1),x^(p-2),x^(p-3). For the next one, the homogeneous high part
of L_n R=P_n/9 gives

    r_(d-2)/r_d=-d(d-1)/[2(2d-1)]=5/21 modulo p.

Here d=-2/3 modulo p and d-2>n in every original case m>=2.
Write S(r)=4r^3(1-3/(4r^2)). At x^(p-4), only S^d and S^(d-2)
contribute, so

    U_(p-4)/u
      = -binom(d,3)*27/64+(5/21)/16
      = 5/24+5/336
      = 25/112.

Thus the p-4 coefficient of (1-x)Z_R' is

    -3k(5u/16)+4k(25u/112)=-5ku/112.                 (1)

## The needed actual-source row

For the original H=h(rho), rho=x(4x-3)^2, with h's Gauss parameters
(-m,-2m;-3m) and leading H coefficient g, the ratio of h's last two
coefficients is

    h_(m-1)/h_m=-m(2m+1)/(m+1)=2/15 modulo p.

The top cubic power rho^m contributes 7/96 at the third lower x-row;
the h_(m-1)rho^(m-1) term contributes (2/15)/16=1/120. Therefore

    H_(N-3)=g(7/96+1/120)=13g/160.

The full H_b has no N-3 term since N>=6. The -2(H-H_b) part has
degree<=N-1<p-4. Hence

    [(4x^N-2)(H-H_b)]_(p-4)=13g/40.                  (2)

Combining (1),(2) and ku=(13g-4)/5 gives

    E_(p-4)=(20-247g)/560.                          (3)

## Elimination without exceptional g or division by 53 or 247

Together with the support author's preceding verified row

    E_(p-3)=(4-53g)/80,

the two equations give the exact identity

    53*(560 E_(p-4))-247*(80 E_(p-3))=72.            (4)

Every original prime is at least13, so72 and the row denominators
80,560 are units. The two rows cannot both vanish. No inverse of g,
53,247, a Fermat quotient, endpoint period or unknown boundary is used;
there is no isolated original-prime exception from this elimination.

If the support author confirms the actual Source h normalization and
row calculations, (4) excludes the whole-polynomial primitive identity
for this EXACT top-normalized/origin-normalized R template throughout
the original prime family. It does not kill the new finite spectral
section itself, prove a half-point mismatch, exclude modified templates,
or solve/obstruct the original ell(T)=3Y objective. Do not extend the
class by unrecorded lower corrections to fit the desired target.

This is paper coefficient algebra only, with no prime sample,
scientific program, array generation or old checker run.
